# GitLab MCP Server

> Agent-workflow-optimized GitLab MCP server for projects, merge requests, issues, pipelines, wiki, releases, tags, and milestones. Transports: stdio, SSE, Streamable HTTP. Auth: PAT, local OAuth, MCP OAuth proxy, per-request remote authorization.

- Package: `@zereight/mcp-gitlab`
- Binary: `zereight-mcp-gitlab` (legacy alias: `mcp-gitlab`)
- Node.js: >=20.0.0
- License: MIT
- Source: https://github.com/zereight/gitlab-mcp
- Docs: https://zereight.github.io/gitlab-mcp/
- Registry name: `io.github.zereight/gitlab-mcp`

## Default exposure

The default `core` toolset lists 38 tools. `discover_tools` and `help` are always re-added after every toolset filter, so a default `tools/list` has **40 tools**.

278 tools exist in total: 275 in 24 toolsets + `execute_graphql` + `discover_tools` + `help`. `GITLAB_TOOLSETS=all` enables every discoverable toolset and still does **not** enable the explicit-only `api` toolset. `execute_graphql` is not in a toolset; enable it with `GITLAB_TOOLS=execute_graphql`.

Call `discover_tools` with no arguments to list categories, then pass a category (`pipelines`, `wiki`, `merge_requests`, …) to activate it for the current session.

Measured default `tools/list` size (2026-10-24): 40 tools, 50,682 bytes of JSON. `GITLAB_TOOLSETS=all`: 276 tools, 285,677 bytes.

## Without → With

Without this MCP, agents paste MR URLs and diffs into chat, hunt job logs in the GitLab UI, and re-explain `group/project` every turn.

With this MCP:

1. `list_merge_request_changed_files` for paths only
2. `get_merge_request_file_diff` for 3–5 files per call
3. `create_merge_request_thread` or draft notes for review comments

`project_id` accepts a numeric ID or a URL-encoded path. Example: merge request `!123` in `group/project` → `project_id=group%2Fproject`, `merge_request_iid=123`. Nested groups use `%2F` between every segment.

## Three install paths

### Local IDE

stdio + PAT or local OAuth (`GITLAB_USE_OAUTH=true`).

```bash
read -rs GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN && export GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
claude mcp add gitlab --transport stdio --scope local --env GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN="$GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN" --env GITLAB_API_URL=https://gitlab.com/api/v4 -- zereight-mcp-gitlab
codex mcp add gitlab --env GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN="$GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN" --env GITLAB_API_URL=https://gitlab.com/api/v4 -- zereight-mcp-gitlab
```

Cursor: use the deeplink in the repository README or [Cursor setup](clients/cursor.md).

Other clients: [VS Code](clients/vscode.md), [Copilot](clients/copilot.md), [JSON clients](clients/json-clients.md).

### Shared HTTP

Hosted or self-hosted Streamable HTTP:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gitlab": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Per-user PAT: `REMOTE_AUTHORIZATION=true` and `Authorization: Bearer` / `Private-Token`.
Claude.ai / remote OAuth: `GITLAB_MCP_OAUTH=true` on a public HTTPS URL.

### Claude.ai

Public HTTPS MCP server + pre-registered GitLab OAuth app + `GITLAB_MCP_OAUTH=true` + `STREAMABLE_HTTP=true`. No PAT in the client config.

## Skill + CLI (equal path, no MCP)

```bash
npx skills add zereight/gitlab-mcp --skill gitlab-mcp-skill
zereight-mcp-gitlab user whoami
zereight-mcp-gitlab mr list
```

Human CLI is never compacted. Destructive tools and `GITLAB_TOOL_POLICY_APPROVE` tools need `--yes`. See [CLI without MCP](getting-started/cli-without-mcp.md).

## MCP vs Human CLI

Use MCP when the agent needs structured tools in chat and `jmespath` / compact results are enough.

Use the CLI when you need the full payload (diffs, job logs, artifacts), or when `GITLAB_MCP_COMPACT_RESULTS=true` has replaced an oversized MCP reply with a preview plus a CLI command.

## Token-saving rules

- Do not dump a full merge request with `get_merge_request_diffs` when file-by-file review is the goal.
- Prefer `jmespath` on tool calls. Enable `GITLAB_MCP_COMPACT_RESULTS` to cap oversized MCP replies.
- Paginate pipeline / job logs (`get_pipeline_job_output`).
- Prefer typed REST tools over `execute_graphql`.
- Do not enable `gitlab_api_request` (`api` toolset) unless you accept that it bypasses group/project allowlists, other tool filters, and per-tool safety checks. Prompt injection can drive it.

## Auth FAQ

- Local PAT: `GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` or `GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE`
- Local OAuth: `GITLAB_USE_OAUTH=true` (browser on the same machine as the server)
- MCP OAuth: public HTTPS server, clients such as Claude.ai
- Remote authorization: caller sends PAT or job token; no OAuth dance
- Permission: `GITLAB_PERMISSION_MODE=readonly|modify|full` (default `full`)

## Cursor / CLAUDE.md snippet

```
GitLab merge requests, issues, and pipelines go through this MCP (@zereight/mcp-gitlab).
Start with the default core tools. Call discover_tools to expand.
Prefer list_merge_request_changed_files, then batched get_merge_request_file_diff.
Use jmespath or compact results; use the CLI for full diffs and job logs.
```
